questions.question: You must use your low beams when you are:

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn yield on green.
One-way.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that they must yield to oncoming traffic when turning left on a green light. You can turn left when it is safe.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from your seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Don't depend only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: You are in a line of cars waiting at a stop sign. After the cars ahead pass through and there is no cross traffic, you should:

options.text: Go through the intersection without stopping again.
Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going.
Slowly roll past the stop sign.
Follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at the stop sign and check for traffic before going. Don't skip stopping just because other cars are moving.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and a siren is approaching. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or a siren, finish crossing the intersection. Then drive to the right side of the road and stop. You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles.

questions.question: On long trips, you can avoid drowsiness by:

options.text: Turning on your car radio.
Slowing down.
Stopping at regular times to rest.
Moving your eyes side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping at regular times to rest.
questions.explanation: On long trips, stop regularly to rest and stretch. Do this even if you don't feel tired.

questions.question: At night, you can use parking lights instead of headlights.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You cannot drive at night using only parking lights. You must use headlights when driving in low light.

questions.question: On a two-way, two-lane street, you cannot pass safely unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle is fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass safely on a two-way street unless you can see the road clearly, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Only pass when it is legal and safe.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Big trucks and SUVs have areas near their rear that you cannot see in mirrors.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road. At 35 mph and below, most tires move water away from the tire. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide like water skis.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road widens ahead.
The right lane is ending soon.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.
The left lane is ending soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending soon.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your right-of-way.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down so the other driver has room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other driver has room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them enough room in front of your vehicle to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing must remain stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving again.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving again.
questions.explanation: You must stay stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus begins moving.

questions.question: When driving across a railroad track with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping on the tracks.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto the tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: You must use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: They are deaf.
They are a police officer.
They are blind.
They have poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red traffic light without stopping. You should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Follow a police officer's directions. They override all traffic signals and signs.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Nothing else, including eating or drinking, speeds up this process.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, yield to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: Vehicles should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes distorted.
You are less alert.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time, reduces vision, distorts judgment of speed and distance, reduces recovery from headlight glare, and increases risk-taking behavior.

questions.question: What does excessive speed do?

options.text: It does not increase the chance of a crash.
It improves your ability to react to danger.
It leads to risky driving decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It leads to risky driving decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed causes many vehicle crashes. It does not save time and often causes drivers to make risky decisions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn allowed.
No left turn allowed.
No right turn allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Turning right here is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and be careful. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians before crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on this narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead has one-way traffic only.
Only one car can use the bridge at a time.
The bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers to be careful. It warns that the bridge ahead may not be wide enough to safely pass a truck.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses grip on wet road, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a steady speed to get better grip.
Push the brakes hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your tires lose contact with the road and slide on water, this is called hydroplaning. Slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other dangerous conditions. Winter driving is difficult and requires extra care. Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels. Snow tires help your vehicle grip icy roads better.

questions.question: When turning or stopping in rain, be most careful:

options.text: After it has rained all day.
Half an hour after rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. Car oil on the road mixes with rain, making the surface slippery.

questions.question: Which statement about passing is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and check for oncoming traffic.
Use mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your mirror before moving back.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before passing. Check mirrors and look over your shoulder. Move back into your lane only after you see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must let all oncoming traffic pass first. This includes cars, motorcycles, and bicycles.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual sights:

options.text: Causes traffic jams.
Stops rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic jams.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at accidents or anything unusual. This causes traffic jams. Avoid "rubbernecking."
